result:
Review complete. Verdict written to `review-verdict.json`: **approve** (tier2, requires human sign-off before merge, per the dispatch prompt's tiered trust model).

Summary: the HR gap-closure work (expense reimbursement, employee loans, KRA/360 appraisal, shift roster) is architecturally sound — clean additive migration with correctly-applied RLS matching the existing convention, correct and idempotent payroll integration (loan deduction/expense-reimbursement earning line, guarded by the existing draft-only re-processing check), and tests for the core pure-function logic. No `.github/workflows/**` changes, so the hard rule doesn't apply.

Two issues flagged for the human reviewer (not blocking, but worth attention):
1. `requestLoan()` lets any employee create a loan request naming an arbitrary coworker as the beneficiary, with no ownership check or manager-role gate — inconsistent with this same PR's own expense-claim pattern (self-service only).
2. Expense/loan list endpoints expose all-employee financial data to any authenticated org member when no filter is passed — this mirrors a pre-existing repo convention (same as leave-requests), so not a new regression, but worth reconsidering given the sensitivity of amounts.
